facts: The research article was published in Frontiers in Computer Science in 2025.
The survey focuses on Large Language Models and their applications in Natural Language Processing.
The authors are affiliated with Central South University, Harbin Institute of Technology, University of Hong Kong, Tsinghua University, and University of Illinois at Chicago.
The research represents a collaborative effort across five leading computer science research centers in China, Hong Kong, and the United States.
This study provides an overview of Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT in Natural Language Processing.
The research addresses three key questions regarding LLMs in NLP literature.
A unified taxonomy of two paradigms—parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning—is introduced in the study.
The work aims to offer practical insights into the potential and limitations of LLMs in NLP applications.
This paper presents the first comprehensive survey of Large Language Models (LLMs) for Natural Language Processing tasks.
LLMs like GPT-series, PaLM-series, OPT, and LLaMA have demonstrated remarkable capabilities through scaling.
The authors propose a novel taxonomy organizing LLM applications into parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
The work provides curated resources including open-source implementations, corpora, and research papers for the LLM-for-NLP research community.
The parameter-frozen paradigm includes zero-shot learning and few-shot learning.
Zero-shot learning offers maximum efficiency and generalization but lower accuracy.
Full-parameter tuning achieves the best in-domain performance but requires high resources.
Parameter-efficient tuning methods like LoRA and QLoRA adjust only selected parameters.
Sentiment Analysis uses zero-shot and few-shot learning with instruction tuning to identify emotional tone in text.
Information Extraction employs zero-shot prompting and decomposition strategies to extract structured information from plain text.
Dialogue Understanding utilizes zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting and agent-based frameworks for task performance.
LoRA is a method used for full-parameter and parameter-efficient tuning to enhance performance in various natural language understanding tasks.
LLMs like GPT-3 achieve strong zero-shot performance in summarization through instruction tuning.
Specialized models such as CodeLLama and CodeGemma demonstrate robust zero-shot capabilities in code generation.
Few-shot learning techniques like "Chain of Density" prompting enhance summary quality.
Reinforcement learning approaches like CodeRL leverage compiler feedback for code refinement.
Multilingual LLMs aim to extend English-centric LLM success to over 7,000 languages.
Multi-modal LLMs require improvements in complex reasoning and effective modal interaction mechanisms.
Hallucination mitigation addresses LLMs' tendency to produce outputs deviating from factual knowledge.
Long Chain-of-Thought extends reasoning capabilities through hierarchical, reflective problem-solving.
Libo Qin et al. led a comprehensive survey on Large Language Models in Natural Language Processing.
The survey introduces a unified taxonomy distinguishing parameter-frozen and parameter-tuning paradigms.
Key techniques covered in the survey include prompt engineering and chain-of-thought reasoning.
Emerging research frontiers highlighted in the survey include multilingual LLM capabilities and autonomous agents.
